_comment: One file for this storefront's policy. Copy to store.json and point STORE_FILE at it,
or leave it at the repository root where CoreYard finds it by default.
Every section is optional, and an absent section means CoreYard's neutral default.
Keys beginning with an underscore are comments; JSON has none.
The individual STORE_*_FILE settings still work and still win, so a site that already
has four separate files does not have to change anything.
What this yard is willing to claim about a part. The defaults state only what the
yard data supports: used, OEM, off an inventoried donor vehicle. They deliberately
do not say every part was tested or inspected, because that is not true at every
yard and a tool must not put a claim in a seller's mouth.
See coreyard/profile.py for every key and its default.
Estimated packed shipping weights by part type, used when the source system has no
weight. Absent means CoreYard estimates nothing and Shopify sees no weight.
How each part ships, and the tag that tells the storefront so.
What closes a storefront order. The default is tag-and-note only, because whether
creating a fulfillment is correct depends on the site's shipping arrangements:
fulfilling under a shipping app that has not bought the label yet costs the buyer
their tracking number, and never fulfilling leaves the order open forever.
